mainTopic: Anointing kings and כהנים, good signs, and who counts as the כהן משיח of our משנה.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא said that יהואחז was anointed as king. Now it asks how that could be, since a ברייתא teaches that יאשיהו hid the שמן המשחה together with the ארון. רב פפא answers that יהואחז was anointed with pure balsam oil. Next come the details of anointing: kings get a crown shape and כהנים get the shape of the Greek letter chi. Two ברייתות disagree about whether pouring on the head or smearing between the eyes comes first. A story about oil drops on אהרן's beard follows, and a בת קול tells משה and אהרן that neither committed מעילה. Kings are anointed by a spring as a good sign, and this opens a list of signs: tests for life, business, and travel, אביי's ראש השנה foods, רב משרשיא's advice to his sons, and anointing from a horn. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה. It defines the כהן משיח and shows that our משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי מאיר, about the כהן גדול appointed only by wearing the extra garments.

steps.title: Was the anointing oil even around?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that יהואחז was anointed, using a ברייתא saying the שמן המשחה was hidden together with the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there anointing oil then? Doesn't a ברייתא teach that when the ארון was hidden, the anointing oil, the jar of מן, אהרן's staff with its almonds and blossoms, and the chest the פלשתים sent as a gift were hidden too? As the פסוק says: 'And the gold vessels that you return to Him as a guilt-offering, put in the chest by its side, and send it away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how יהואחז could have been anointed, since a ברייתא says the שמן המשחה was hidden away before his time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said יהואחז was anointed. But if the שמן המשחה was hidden together with the ארון, there was no holy oil left to anoint him with. The פסוק about the chest 'by its side' shows that the chest stayed next to the ארון, so it was hidden with it too.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy anointing oil made by משה
The jar of מן kept as a reminder

phrases.english: And was there anointing oil?
phrases.notes: He means in the days of יהואחז, who the גמרא just said was anointed.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: once the Ark was hidden away,
the anointing oil and the jar of manna were hidden away,
and Aaron's staff with its almonds and blossoms,
and the chest that the Philistines sent as a gift to Israel,
as it is said: "And the vessels of gold
phrases.notes: שמואל א ו:ח

phrases.english: that you return to Him as a guilt-offering,
put in the chest by its side,
phrases.notes: 'Its side' means next to the ארון. That is why the chest was hidden along with it.

phrases.english: and send it off, and it will go."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier statement on the daf that יהואחז was anointed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יהואחז was anointed with oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the שמן המשחה was hidden together with the ארון, so it was not available to anoint יהואחז.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether יהואחז was a real king. It is only about what oil they could have used to anoint him.

steps.title: יאשיהו hid the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: יאשיהו hid the ארון because he feared exile, and the פסוק in דברי הימים shows he ordered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who hid it? יאשיהו king of יהודה hid it. He saw that the תורה says: 'ה׳ will lead you and your king to a nation you have not known.' So he commanded, and they hid them, as it says: 'He said to the לויים who taught all ישראל, who were holy to ה׳: Put the holy ארון in the house that שלמה son of דוד king of ישראל built. You no longer have to carry it on your shoulders. Now serve ה׳ your God and His people ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and explains who hid the ארון and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיהו saw the warning that ישראל and its king would go into exile, so he hid the ארון to protect it from being taken. Since יאשיהו came before יהואחז, the oil was already hidden in יהואחז's time, which makes the challenge stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous king of יהודה, the father of יהואחז
A burden carried on the shoulder

phrases.english: And who hid it?
Josiah, king of Judah, hid it,
because he saw that it is written in the Torah:
"The Lord will lead you and your king, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים כח:לו. The rest of the פסוק says they will be taken to a foreign nation.

phrases.english: he commanded and they hid them, as it is said:
"And he said to the Levites who taught all Israel,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב לה:ג

phrases.english: who were holy to the Lord:
Place the holy Ark in the house

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה בֶן דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built;
you have no burden on the shoulder;
now serve the Lord your God
and His people Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי גְּנָזוֹ? יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה גְּנָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא used in the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יאשיהו ordered that the ארון be hidden because he feared the exile that the תורה warned about.

steps.title: Matching words link all the hidden items
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses three גזירות שוות to show that the מן, the staff, and the oil were all hidden together with the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: we learn 'there' from 'there', 'keepsake' from 'keepsake', and 'generations' from 'generations'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי אלעזר's source showing that the oil really was hidden with the ארון. This finishes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'there' links the ארון to the jar of מן. The word 'keepsake' links the מן to אהרן's staff. The word 'generations' links the מן to the שמן המשחה. So the oil goes wherever the ארון goes, and the question is now very strong: what oil did they use for יהואחז?

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from. This is shorthand for a גזירה שוה, learning from a matching word.
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
A keepsake, something to be guarded

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
"There" is learned from "there",
phrases.notes: This ties the ארון to the jar of מן, since both are described with the word 'there'.

phrases.english: "keepsake" is learned from "keepsake",
"generations" is learned from "generations"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the ברייתא's claim that all these items were hidden with the ארון, which completes the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That the שמן המשחה was hidden together with the ארון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three גזירות שוות: שם, משמרת, דורות.

steps.title: יהואחז was anointed with balsam
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that יהואחז was anointed with pure balsam oil, not with the real שמן המשחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: with pure balsam oil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. They anointed יהואחז with a different, fine oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא explains that יהואחז never got the holy שמן המשחה; he was anointed with pure balsam oil instead. That way the ברייתא is true, since the holy oil was hidden, and so is the statement that יהואחז was anointed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
With pure balsam oil.
phrases.notes: He means that is what they used to anoint יהואחז, not the holy oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 1 to 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the anointing used a different oil.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed that anointing יהואחז meant using the real שמן המשחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was anointed with pure balsam oil, so there is no conflict with the oil being hidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The שמן המשחה was hidden along with the ארון by יאשיהו. Later kings like יהואחז were anointed with pure balsam oil instead.

steps.title: The shapes of anointing for kings and כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that kings are anointed in the shape of a crown and כהנים in the shape of a 'כי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How do we anoint kings? In the shape of a crown. And כהנים? In the shape of a 'כי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about the shape in which the oil is put on kings and on כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kings get the oil around the head like a crown. כהנים get it in a different shape, called 'כי'. The next step will explain what 'כי' means.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How does one anoint the kings?
In a shape like a crown.
And the priests? In a shape like a chi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether there was anointing oil to how the anointing was done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings are anointed in a crown shape; כהנים in a 'כי' shape.

steps.title: What does 'like a כי' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shape 'כי' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like a כי' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unclear word in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כי' is not a familiar shape, so the גמרא wants to know exactly how the oil was placed on the כהן.

phrases.english: What is "in a shape like a chi"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term in the ברייתא from step 5.

steps.title: It means the Greek letter that matches כ
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר גדא explains that 'כי' is the Greek letter matching the Hebrew כ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר גדא said: like a Greek כ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא בר גדא answers that 'כי' is a Greek letter, the Greek version of our letter כ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כי' is not a Hebrew word here. It is the name of a Greek letter, chi, which sounds like the Hebrew כ. So the oil on a כהן was put on in the shape of that letter.

keyTerms.meaning: The Greek kaf, the Greek letter chi

phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Gadda said:
In a shape like a Greek kaf.
phrases.notes: The Greek letter chi is written like an X.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא: כְּמִין כָּף יְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי' is the Greek letter that matches the Hebrew כ.
steps.whatToRemember: Kings are anointed in a crown shape around the head. כהנים are anointed in the shape of the Greek letter chi.

steps.title: Two teachings give opposite orders for anointing
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says pour oil on the head first and then smear between the eyelashes. Another ברייתא says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teaching says: first they pour oil on his head, then they put oil between his eyelashes. Another teaching says: first they put oil between his eyelashes, then they pour oil on his head!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side and shows that they contradict each other about the order of anointing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachings agree that there are two actions: יציקה (pouring on the head) and משיחה (smearing between the eyelashes). They disagree only about which comes first. The exclamation mark shows the גמרא is pointing out a real clash.

phrases.english: It is taught in one ברייתא:
First, they pour oil on his head,
phrases.notes: "His" means the כהן being anointed.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹתְנִין לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו.
phrases.english: and afterward they place oil for him between his eyelashes.
And it is taught in a different ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: בַּתְּחִלָּה נוֹתְנִין לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו,
phrases.english: First, they place oil for him between his eyelashes,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מוֹצְקִים לוֹ שֶׁמֶן עַל רֹאשׁוֹ!
phrases.english: and afterward they pour oil on his head!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of how כהנים are anointed and raises a contradiction about the order.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about the order of anointing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two authoritative teachings cannot both be right about which action comes first.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות reflect two opinions. One holds smearing is more important, the other holds pouring is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים. Some say smearing is more important, and some say pouring is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two teachings come from different תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side does the more important action first. Whoever ranks משיחה higher puts the eyelashes first, and whoever ranks יציקה higher puts the head first. This sets up the next question: what is each side's reason?

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Smearing or anointing (the oil between the eyes)

phrases.english: It is a dispute between תנאים.
Some say: smearing is preferable,
and some say: pouring is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the contradicting sources to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות were thought to follow one view, so they clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow two opinions about which action is more important.

steps.title: Why is pouring more important?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the view that יציקה is preferable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says pouring is preferable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first opinion and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that there are two opinions, the גמרא wants to see what each one is built on, starting with the pouring view.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who says
that pouring is preferable?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יְצִיקָה עֲדִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of one side of the dispute in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for ranking יציקה first

steps.title: The פסוק says pouring and then anointing
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about אהרן mentions pouring first and anointing after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And he poured from the anointing oil on אהרן's head, and anointed him to sanctify him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק where pouring comes before anointing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the words in the פסוק is taken as the order of importance. "ויצק" comes first, so pouring comes first.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּצֹק מִשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה עַל רֹאשׁ אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: As it is written: "And he poured from the anointing oil on אהרן's head
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:12

phrases.english: and anointed him to sanctify him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק lists pouring before anointing.

steps.title: Why is anointing more important?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the view that משיחה is preferable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says smearing is preferable, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the reason of the second opinion and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view seems harder to defend, because the פסוק just quoted puts pouring first. So the גמרא needs to hear his reason.

phrases.english: And the one who says smearing is preferable,
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיחָה עֲדִיפָא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the other side of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for ranking משיחה first

steps.title: Learning from the כלי שרת
steps.stepSummary: He learns from the כלי שרת, which were only anointed and never had oil poured on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds this because that is what you find with the כלי שרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second view's reason: the holy vessels were made holy through משיחה alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels show that anointing by itself makes something holy. So anointing is the main act and should come first.

keyTerms.meaning: The vessels used in the holy service

phrases.english: He holds: because that is what you find
phrases.notes: The vessels were anointed but had no oil poured on them (see במדבר 7:1).

phrases.english: with the כלי שרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר שֶׁכֵּן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֵצֶל כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כלי שרת were sanctified by anointing alone, so anointing is primary.

steps.title: But the פסוק puts pouring first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משיחה view: the פסוק says "ויצק" first and "וימשח" only at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written "and he poured," and only at the end "and anointed"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second view using the same פסוק the first view relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If anointing is more important, why does the פסוק describe pouring first? The order of the פסוק seems to go against the משיחה view.

phrases.english: But isn't it written "and he poured,"
and only at the end "and anointed"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 13 using the פסוק from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that משיחה is preferable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's order puts pouring before anointing.

steps.title: Pouring happened because of the anointing
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is read differently: the pouring was done because he had already anointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: why did he pour? Because he had anointed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the משיחה view by rereading the פסוק so that anointing is the main act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וימשח" is not the next step in time. It explains why the pouring was done. So anointing stays the main act, and the פסוק no longer goes against this view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

steps.whatToRemember: One view says pouring on the head comes first, learned from the order of the פסוק. The other says anointing between the eyes comes first, learned from the כלי שרת, and reads the פסוק as "he poured because he anointed."

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
What is the reason "he poured"?
Because "he anointed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's word order shows pouring is first in importance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pouring was done because of the anointing, so anointing is primary.

steps.title: Two pearl-like drops on אהרן's beard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the פסוק in תהלים: two drops of oil shaped like pearls hung from אהרן's beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "Like the good oil coming down on the beard, אהרן's beard": two drops like pearls hung from אהרן's beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about the anointing oil on אהרן and describes two drops that stayed on his beard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes oil coming down on אהרן's beard. The ברייתא says that two drops stayed hanging there like pearls. This detail sets up the worries that follow.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Like the good oil, and so on,
phrases.notes: תהלים 133:2. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; וגו׳ means the פסוק keeps going.

phrases.aramaic: יֹרֵד עַל הַזָּקָן זְקַן אַהֲרֹן וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: coming down on the beard, אהרן's beard, and so on":
something like two drops shaped like pearls
were hanging for אהרן on his beard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of anointing to an אגדה about the oil on אהרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two pearl-like drops of anointing oil stayed on אהרן's beard.

steps.title: The drops rose to the roots of his beard
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds a teaching: when אהרן spoke, the drops went up and settled at the roots of his beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said it was taught: when he would speak, they would rise and settle at the roots of his beard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a detail to the story: the drops never fell off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drops did not drip away even when his beard moved. That is why extra holy oil stayed on אהרן permanently, which leads to משה's worry.

phrases.english: רב פפא said, it was taught:
When he speaks,
phrases.notes: When אהרן talked, his beard moved, yet the drops still didn't fall.

phrases.english: they rise and settle at the roots of his beard,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the description of the drops in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The drops stayed on the beard and never fell.

steps.title: משה worries he committed מעילה
steps.stepSummary: משה worried that the extra drops meant he had misused the holy anointing oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And משה was worried about this. He said: perhaps, God forbid, I misused the anointing oil?
steps.whatsHappening: The story raises a worry: maybe משה did something wrong with the holy oil. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using holy property for no holy purpose is מעילה. משה was the one who poured, so he feared the leftover drops showed he had poured too much and wasted holy oil.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה דּוֹאֵג,
phrases.english: And about this matter משה was worried.
He said: perhaps, God forbid,
I misused the anointing oil?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה דּוֹאֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a halachic concern caused by the drops of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the leftover holy oil means משה committed מעילה

steps.title: A בת קול: like the dew of חרמון, no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול compares the oil to the dew of חרמון. Just as dew is not holy, the oil on אהרן's beard carries no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said: "Like the good oil... like the dew of חרמון." Just as the dew of חרמון has no מעילה, so too the anointing oil on אהרן's beard has no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A heavenly voice calms משה by showing from the פסוק that the oil on the beard is not a case of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק puts the oil next to the dew of חרמון. Dew is ordinary, so nobody can commit מעילה with it. The oil on the beard is treated the same way.

phrases.english: A בת קול came out and said:
"Like the good oil, and so on, like the dew of חרמון."
phrases.notes: תהלים 133:2-3

phrases.aramaic: מָה טַל חֶרְמוֹן אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: Just as the dew of חרמון has no מעילה,
so too the anointing oil on אהרן's beard
has no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's worry in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oil on the beard is like the dew of חרמון, with no מעילה.

steps.title: אהרן worries that he committed מעילה
steps.stepSummary: אהרן still worried: maybe משה is fine, but אהרן himself misused the oil by having it on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still אהרן was worried. He said: perhaps משה did not commit מעילה, but I did?
steps.whatsHappening: The story raises a second worry, this time from אהרן. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's question was about the pouring. אהרן's question is different: the oil stays on his own beard, so maybe he is the one benefiting from holy oil.

phrases.english: And still אהרן was worried.
He said: perhaps משה did not commit מעילה,
but I did commit מעילה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new worry that the answer of step 19 did not seem to cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אהרן, who carries the oil, committed מעילה

steps.title: Like brothers together: you did not commit מעילה either
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול quotes "how good and pleasant for brothers to dwell together." Just as משה did not commit מעילה, neither did אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said to him: "Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together." Just as משה did not commit מעילה, so too you did not.
steps.whatsHappening: A heavenly voice calms אהרן by joining him to his brother משה: both are free of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "together" in the פסוק links the brothers. Whatever is true for משה is true for אהרן, so the answer that cleared משה clears אהרן too.
steps.whatToRemember: The oil drops on אהרן's beard were not מעילה, neither for משה who poured them nor for אהרן who carried them. The proofs come from the פסוקים in תהלים קל״ג.

phrases.english: A בת קול came out and said to him:
"Behold how good and how pleasant
phrases.notes: תהלים 133:1

phrases.english: is the dwelling of brothers together."
Just as משה did not commit מעילה,
so too you did not commit מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אהרן's worry in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The brothers are linked, so like משה, אהרן did not commit מעילה.

steps.title: Kings are anointed by a spring
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that kings are anointed only beside a spring, as a sign that their kingdom will continue, based on the anointing of שלמה at גיחון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: kings are anointed only by a spring, so their rule will last, as the פסוק says: 'Take your lord's servants and bring him down to גיחון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying kings are anointed next to a spring. It proves this from the anointing of שלמה at גיחון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spring keeps flowing without stopping, so anointing there acts as a good sign that the king's rule will keep going too. The proof is that דוד sent שלמה down to גיחון, a spring, to be anointed. This also opens the theme of סימנים that fills the rest of this section.

keyTerms.meaning: so that their kingdom will continue

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the starting point for the idea that a סימן, a sign, can have real meaning. אביי builds on that idea at the end of the section.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One does not anoint the kings
except beside a spring,
so that their kingdom will continue,
as it is said:
"And the king said to them:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:33. The king speaking is דוד, about anointing שלמה.

phrases.english: Take with you the servants of your lord [etc.]
and bring him down to Gihon."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מוֹשְׁחִים אֶת הַמְּלָכִים אֶלָּא עַל הַמַּעְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of the anointing oil on אהרן's beard to a related anointing law about kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings are anointed only beside a spring, as a sign that their rule will last; the source is שלמה's anointing at גיחון.

steps.title: The lamp test for a long life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says that someone who wants to know if he will live through the year can light a lamp in a windless house during the עשרת ימי תשובה and see if it keeps burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: if someone wants to know whether he will live through the year, he should hang a lamp during the ten days between ראש השנה and יום כפור in a house with no wind. If the light keeps going, he will know he will finish the year.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just mentioned a good sign, it brings רבי אמי's list of folk signs. This first one is about whether a person will live through the coming year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamp that keeps burning stands for a life that keeps going. The test is done in the days between ראש השנה and יום כפור, when the year's judgment is decided, and in a windless house so only the sign itself decides whether the flame goes out.

keyTerms.meaning: finishes his year (stays alive through the year)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
One who wants to know
whether he will finish his year or not,
phrases.notes: He means whether he will stay alive through the coming year.

phrases.english: let him hang up a lamp

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲשָׂרָה יוֹמֵי דְּבֵין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
phrases.english: during the ten days between Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur
in a house where the wind does not blow.
If its light keeps going,
he will know that he will finish his year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לִידַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the theme of signs from the king's anointing to signs about a person's own year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamp that keeps burning in a windless house during the עשרת ימי תשובה is a sign that the person will live through the year.

steps.title: The rooster test for business success
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבי אמי's list: someone starting a business can raise a rooster; if it grows fat and healthy, he will succeed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to start a business and wants to know if he will succeed should raise a rooster. If it gets fat and healthy, he will succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes on with a second sign, this one about whether a business will succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the sign is growth: a rooster that grows fat and healthy stands for a business that grows and does well. The pattern is the same as the lamp, where something that keeps going or grows points to a good outcome.

phrases.english: And one who wants to go into a business deal,
and wants to know
whether he will succeed or not succeed,
let him raise a rooster.
If it grows fat and healthy, he will succeed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in רבי אמי's list of signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rooster that grows fat and healthy is a sign that the business will succeed.

steps.title: The shadow test for a safe return home
steps.stepSummary: Third sign: before a trip, a person can stand in a dark house. If he sees the shadow of a shadow, he will come home safely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to go on a trip and wants to know if he will come back home should stand in a dark house. If he sees the shadow of his shadow, he will know he will return home.
steps.whatsHappening: The list ends with a third sign, this one about whether a traveler will come home safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This test checks whether the person can make out even a faint shadow of his shadow in a dark room. Seeing it is the good sign that he will come back home. The next step questions whether anyone should do these tests at all.

phrases.english: One who wants to set out [on a journey]
and wants to know
whether he will return and come home or not,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. Both mean 'return.'

phrases.english: let him stand in a dark house,
phrases.notes: Here דחברא is read as 'dark.' Some understand it as 'a friend's house.'

phrases.english: if he sees the shadow of a shadow,
let him know that he will return and come home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the list of signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the shadow of a shadow in a dark house is a sign that the traveler will return home.

steps.title: Warning: these tests can backfire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says these tests are not reliable and should not be done. If the sign comes out badly, the person may lose heart, and that alone can harm his מזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not something to do, because if it doesn't work out he may become discouraged, and his luck will be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on actually doing these tests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רש״י explains that the sign itself cannot be relied on. Beyond that, the worry is what a bad result does to the person: once he loses heart, his מזל can drop, so the test itself can cause the failure he was afraid of.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not a proper thing (to do)

steps.confusionAlert: This line says two things. Per רש״י, the test is not reliable, since sometimes a person comes home even without seeing the shadow. And even so, it should not be done, because losing heart can harm his מזל.

phrases.english: But this is nothing to rely on,
since perhaps he will become discouraged,
and his fortune will be harmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִלְּתָא הִיא, דִּלְמָא חָלְשָׁא דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects putting the three tests from רבי אמי's list into practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects doing the tests in practice, not the idea that signs have meaning.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A bad result can discourage the person, and that discouragement itself harms his מזל.

steps.title: אביי: see fast-growing foods on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that since a סימן does matter, a person should get used to seeing squash, fenugreek, leeks, chard, and dates on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: now that you have said a sign is meaningful, a person should always be used to seeing, at the start of the year, squash, fenugreek, leeks, chard, and dates.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the idea that signs matter and turns it into a positive practice for ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of risky tests that could turn out badly, אביי suggests a sign that can only help: seeing foods that grow quickly and plentifully, as a good start to the new year. This is the source of the סימנים many people eat at the ראש השנה meal.

keyTerms.meaning: the start of the year, ראש השנה

steps.whatToRemember: Signs matter. Kings are anointed by a spring, but testing your own future can backfire. The safe way to use a סימן is אביי's: seeing foods that grow quickly on ראש השנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source in the גמרא for the ראש השנה סימנים, a practice still kept today.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Now that you have said that a sign is meaningful,
a person should [always] be used to seeing
at the start of the year
squash and fenugreek,
leeks, chard, and dates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ סִימָנָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that signs matter and directs it to a safe, positive practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה, a person should get used to seeing squash, fenugreek, leeks, chard, and dates as good signs for the year.

steps.title: How to learn before your teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא tells his sons to prepare before going to their רבי, to watch his mouth while he teaches, and to review beside a flowing river.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to his sons: Before you go in to learn from your teacher, review the teaching first. When you sit before him, look at his mouth, as the פסוק says, 'Your eyes shall see your teacher.' When you review, do it beside a river, so that just as the water keeps flowing, your learning will keep flowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the theme of good signs with practical advice from רב משרשיא about learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives three tips: prepare first, watch the teacher closely, and review beside flowing water. The river tip is a good sign of the same kind as the foods in אביי's list: the flowing water hints that your learning will keep flowing.

phrases.english: רב משרשיא said to his sons:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי בָּעֵיתוּ מֵיעַל וּמִיגְמַרי קַמֵּי רַבַּיְיכוּ,
phrases.english: When you want to go in and learn before your teacher,
review the teaching first
and then go in before your teacher.
And when you sit before him,
look at his mouth,
as it is written: 'And your eyes shall see your teacher.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:20

phrases.english: And when you review,
review beside a river of water,
so that just as the water keeps flowing,
your learning will keep flowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's idea that a סימן matters, now applied to learning Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prepare before learning, watch the teacher's mouth, and review beside flowing water as a good sign that the learning will flow.

steps.title: A simple place is better than a fancy one
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא adds that it is better to sit on the trash heaps of מתא מחסיא than in the palaces of פומבדיתא, and better to eat its poor fish than a rich, strong dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sit on the trash heaps of מתא מחסיא, and do not sit in the palaces of פומבדיתא. Eating the rotten little fish of מתא מחסיא is better than eating כותחא so strong it splits rocks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא keeps advising his sons, this time about where to live and learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses two sharp contrasts: trash heaps against palaces, and rotten fish against a rich, powerful dish. Each time he chooses the simple life in מתא מחסיא over the comfort of פומבדיתא.

phrases.english: And sit on the trash heaps of מתא מחסיא,
and do not sit in the palaces of פומבדיתא.
Better the rotten little fish
of מתא מחסיא to eat
phrases.notes: Not every version has the words in square brackets. They are part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: than כותחא that splits rocks.
phrases.notes: 'Splits rocks' is a picture of how strong and rich this dish is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב משרשיא's advice to his sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble life in מתא מחסיא is better than luxury in פומבדיתא.

steps.title: Anointing from a horn means lasting kingship
steps.stepSummary: From חנה's words 'my horn is raised,' the גמרא shows that kings anointed from a horn had lasting kingship and kings anointed from a jug did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My horn is raised up through my God' means my horn is raised, not my jug. דוד and שלמה were anointed from a horn, and their kingship lasted. שאול and יהוא were anointed from a jug, and their kingship did not last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more good sign, this time about anointing kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names a horn, so the גמרא reads it as excluding a jug. History fits this reading: the kings anointed from a horn had lasting kingship, and the kings anointed from a jug did not. This also leads into the משנה's topic of anointing.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two words that sound alike here. נִמְשְׁחוּ (with ח) means 'anointed,' and נִמְשְׁכָה (with כ) means 'continued.' Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: 'My horn is raised up through my God':
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:1, from חנה's prayer.

phrases.english: 'my horn is raised,' and not 'my jug is raised.'
דוד and שלמה, who were anointed from a horn,
their kingship lasted.
שאול and יהוא, who were anointed from a jug,
their kingship did not last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another good sign, now about anointing, which leads back toward the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anointing from a horn was a sign of lasting kingship, and anointing from a jug was not.
steps.whatToRemember: The section on good signs ends here: lamp, rooster, shadow, foods, a river, and a horn.

steps.title: Which anointed one is the כהן משיח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows from the פסוק that the 'משיח' is a כהן, anointed with oil, and the highest כהן. He is not a king, not a כהן גדול who only wears the extra garments, and not the משוח מלחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'the one anointed with the anointing oil.' The רבנן taught: 'Anointed' might mean a king, so the פסוק says 'כהן.' If it means a כהן, it might be one who only wears the extra garments, so the פסוק says 'anointed.' If it means anointed, it might be the כהן anointed for war, so the פסוק says 'and the anointed כהן,' meaning there is no anointed one above him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and brings a ברייתא that defines exactly who the כהן משיח is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא narrows the meaning step by step. 'כהן' rules out a king. 'משיח' rules out the מרובה בגדים, who became כהן גדול by wearing the eight garments without being anointed. The full phrase 'והכהן המשיח' rules out the משוח מלחמה, because it means the one with no anointed כהן above him.

keyTerms.meaning: a כהן גדול made so by wearing the extra garments, without oil
the כהן anointed to serve the army in war

steps.whyThisMatters: Only this כהן brings the special פר for a mistaken ruling discussed in our מסכת, so it matters exactly who counts.

phrases.english: The one anointed with the anointing oil, etc.
The Rabbis taught: 'Anointed':
could it mean a king?
So the פסוק says 'כהן.'
If it means a כהן, could it be one who only wears the extra garments?
So the פסוק says 'anointed.'
If it means anointed, could it be the כהן anointed for war?
So the פסוק says: 'And the anointed כהן,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:15

phrases.english: meaning there is no anointed one above him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the good-signs discussion and returns to the משנה's definition of the כהן משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן משיח is the כהן גדול anointed with the anointing oil, who has no anointed one above him.

steps.title: How does the word show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'המשיח' teaches that no anointed one is above him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see this in the word?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא gets its last point from the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'המשיח' does not plainly say 'the highest anointed one.' The גמרא wants to know what in the word gives that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: what shows this? how is it implied?

phrases.english: How is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last step of the ברייתא's derivation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'הכהן המשיח' teaches that no anointed כהן is above him.

steps.title: 'The' means the best one
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's reading of 'הירך' as the stronger thigh, the גמרא explains 'המשיח' as the most distinguished of the anointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: 'the thigh' means the stronger of the thighs. Here too, 'the anointed' means the most distinguished of the anointed ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing this word to another פסוק that רבא explained the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read 'הַיָּרֵךְ,' with the word 'the,' as pointing to the best, stronger thigh. In the same way, 'הַמָּשִׁיחַ' points to the top anointed one, the כהן גדול. The משוח מלחמה is anointed too, but he is not the top one, so he is excluded.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן משיח of our משנה is the highest anointed כהן, the כהן גדול anointed with oil.

phrases.english: As רבא said:
'the thigh' means the stronger of the thighs.
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:33, the פסוק about גיד הנשה.

phrases.english: Here too:
'the anointed' means the most distinguished of the anointed ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'the' (ה) points to the best and highest one, just as רבא explained 'הירך'.

steps.title: Why would anyone think the verse means a king?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's idea that 'משיח' might mean a king, because a king brings a goat, not a bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'משיח', you might think it means a king. But does a king bring a bull? A king brings a goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא in step 31 and attacks it. Why would we even think the 'anointed one' who brings a bull could be a king?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself says a king brings a שעיר (male goat) for his sin. So the guess that 'משיח' could mean a king seems pointless, because the bull passage cannot be about him anyway. The challenge is that the ברייתא is ruling out something nobody would think.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think', introduces a possibility that will be rejected
A bull, the special offering of the anointed כהן
A male goat, the sin-offering a king brings

phrases.english: The Master said: 'Anointed', you might think this means a king.
Is it a bull that a king brings?
It is a male goat that he brings!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶלֶךְ פַּר הוּא דְּמַיְיתֵי? שָׂעִיר הוּא דְּמַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 31 and challenges one of its lines.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה explicitly gives a king a goat, so there is no reason to think the bull passage could refer to him.

steps.title: We might have thought a king brings a bull for a mistaken ruling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא was needed. We might have thought a king brings a goat for an ordinary mistake but a bull for a mistaken ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: for a mistaken action he brings a goat, but for a mistaken ruling (העלם דבר) he brings a bull. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The ברייתא had to say the king is not included, because there was a real reason to think he might be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat in the תורה could be only for a plain mistaken action (שגגת מעשה). For the special case of a mistaken ruling (העלם דבר), we might have guessed the king brings a bull like the anointed כהן. The ברייתא teaches that only the כהן brings the bull.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was needed', the teaching is not extra after all
'It could enter your mind to say', introduces the mistaken first thought
A mistaken ruling, where the law itself was forgotten
'It teaches us', the new point being made

steps.whatToRemember: Only the anointed כהן גדול brings the special bull. A king brings a goat even in the case of a mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
as it could enter your mind to say:
for a mistaken action, the king brings a goat,
but for a mistaken ruling, he brings a bull,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a real הוה אמינא that justifies the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A king brings a goat for a mistaken action but a bull for a mistaken ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bull is only for the anointed כהן. A king never brings it.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the כהן גדול anointed with oil and says it does not follow רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: The only difference between a כהן anointed with the anointing oil and one appointed by the extra garments is that the second one does not bring the bull. This משנה does not follow רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and states that it does not match רבי מאיר's view. The next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a כהן גדול appointed only by wearing the eight garments (מרובה בגדים) does not bring the bull for the מצוות. The גמרא claims this is not רבי מאיר's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The special anointing oil used to appoint a כהן גדול
A כהן גדול appointed by wearing the extra garments, without the oil

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: There is no difference between one anointed with the anointing oil, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of the משנה: the one with only the garments does not bring the bull for the מצוות.

phrases.english: Our משנה is not like רבי מאיר,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה, which exempts the מרובה בגדים from the bull, does not follow רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר makes him bring the bull
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי מאיר holds the מרובה בגדים does bring the bull, and the חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it followed רבי מאיר, we learned in a ברייתא: A מרובה בגדים brings the bull for all the מצוות. That is רבי מאיר's view, and the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its claim from step 36 by quoting a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes the garments-only כהן גדול bring the bull, which is the opposite of the משנה. The חכמים disagree, so the משנה must follow the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it was taught', brings a ברייתא as proof
'The חכמים did not agree with him'

phrases.english: for if it were רבי מאיר, it was taught:
one appointed by the extra garments brings a bull
that comes for all the מצוות,
these are the words of רבי מאיר,
and the חכמים did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of step 36.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר obligates the מרובה בגדים in the bull and the חכמים disagree

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי מאיר gets his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of the 'anointed' כהן, which seems to mean only one anointed with oil. So the גמרא wants to know how רבי מאיר includes a כהן גדול who was never anointed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?', asks for the source of an opinion

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion quoted in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind רבי מאיר's view that the מרובה בגדים brings the bull.

steps.title: 'הכהן המשיח' includes the garments-only כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the extra words 'הכהן המשיח' that the מרובה בגדים is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: 'משיח', this only tells me about one anointed with the anointing oil. From where do I know about one appointed by the extra garments? The verse says: 'הכהן המשיח'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives רבי מאיר's source from the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'משיח' alone would cover only someone actually anointed with oil. The fuller phrase 'הכהן המשיח' widens it to include any כהן גדול, even one appointed by the garments alone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have', what we would know without the extra word
'The verse says', brings the words that teach the point

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר learns from 'הכהן המשיח' that even a כהן גדול appointed only by the garments brings the bull. The חכמים disagree, and our משנה follows them.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Anointed'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה,
phrases.english: I only have one anointed with the anointing oil,
from where do I know one appointed by the extra garments?
The verse says: 'The anointed כהן'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״מָשִׁיחַ״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'הכהן המשיח' include the מרובה בגדים.

steps.title: Which opinion does the משנה follow? The חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view it has used to explain the משנה and answers that it is the חכמים. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom did you explain the משנה? Like the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up which opinion the משנה follows: the חכמים. This is a setup for the next move, which will test this against another part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה exempts the garments-only כהן גדול from the bull, it must follow the חכמים and not רבי מאיר. Fixing that point prepares the ground for the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like whom did you set it up?', which opinion was used to explain the משנה
The חכמים, the majority opinion against רבי מאיר

phrases.english: Like whom did you explain it? Like the Rabbis,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the conclusion of steps 36-37 to prepare a new challenge.
